name: Herbert Kociemba — Two-Phase Algorithm & Cube Explorer
zh: Kociemba 两阶段算法 + 立方坐标模型(corner/edge 排列 / twist / flip 编码、面转表):/scramble/solver 的 3×3 两阶段解(含 crz3a 疯狂 3×3)、STM 最优解器的状态编码、cube48opt 服务端最优解器都基于此;Cube Explorer 是已知唯一的 STM 最优解器(参照);/scramble/pattern/search 的图案搜索移植自 Cube Explorer 的 Pattern Editor(PatternSearch.pas);/scramble/symmetry 的对称型搜索与 33 种类型数据移植自 Symmetry Editor(SymSearch.pas + Symmetries.pas + CubeDefs.pas)
en: Kociemba's two-phase algorithm + cube coordinate model (corner/edge perm, twist, flip encoders; face-move tables) underpin the /scramble/solver 3×3 two-phase solve (incl. the crz3a Crazy-3×3 solver), the STM optimal solver's state encoding, and the server-side cube48opt optimal solver; Cube Explorer is the only known prior STM-optimal solver (reference); /scramble/pattern/search ports Cube Explorer's Pattern Editor (PatternSearch.pas), and /scramble/symmetry ports its Symmetry Editor (SymSearch.pas + Symmetries.pas + CubeDefs.pas)
long_en: Herbert Kociemba's two-phase algorithm and the Singmaster cubie coordinate model (corner/edge permutation ranks, corner-twist / edge-flip ranks, face-move arrays — also as ported in cs0x7f's min2phase.js) are the basis of the site's client-side 3×3 two-phase solver (the derive-scramble flow + the crz3a solver), the new pure-TS 3×3×3 STM optimal solver's state encoding (cross-validated against these tables), and the server-side cube48opt optimal-solve daemon. Cube Explorer (kociemba.org) is the only known pre-existing STM-optimal solver — the reference our STM goal-test (centers must end home) follows. The /scramble/pattern/search page is a faithful port of Cube Explorer's Pattern Editor (PatternSearch.pas: abstract face-pattern DFS with color-class bijection matching, continuity check, and isomorphism dedup). The /scramble/symmetry page ports the Symmetry Editor: the 48 symmetry cubie tables of Symmetries.pas, the 33 subgroup bitmasks and per-type position counts of CubeDefs.pas / SymSearch.pas, and the symmetry-constrained DFS of SymSearch.pas (equivariant piece placement, antisymmetry, per-face colour counts, permutation parity modes, exact-symmetry filtering)

name: Richard E. Korf — IDA* + Pattern Databases
zh: Korf 的 IDA* + 模式数据库(AAAI 1997)+ 滑块 walking-distance 启发:STM 最优解器的角表(8!×3⁷)+ 双 6 棱表(12P6×2⁶)、h=max(...) 可采纳启发,数字华容道 15p 的 walking-distance,cube48opt 3×3 最优解都出自此法
en: Korf's IDA* with pattern databases (AAAI 1997) + the sliding-tile walking-distance heuristic: the STM optimal solver's corner PDB (8!×3⁷) + two 6-edge PDBs (12P6×2⁶) with h = max(...), the 15-puzzle (15p) walking-distance optimal solve, and cube48opt's 3×3 optimal solve all use this method
long_en: Richard E. Korf's 'Finding Optimal Solutions to Rubik's Cube Using Pattern Databases' (AAAI 1997) — max/additive pattern-database IDA* — is the method behind the pure-TS 3×3×3 STM optimal solver (corner PDB 8!×3⁷ + two disjoint 6-edge PDBs 12P6×2⁶, admissible h = max of EXACT BFS distances rebuilt over the 27 STM generators) and, via his walking-distance heuristic, the 15-puzzle optimal solver (/scramble/solver 15p); the server-side cube48opt 3×3 optimal-solve daemon is in the same lineage

name: Rubik's Clock 最优求解先行工作(Kogler / Rokicki / OptClock / cs0x7f)
zh: 魔表 God's number = 12 的证明与全空间分析:Jakob Kogler 2014 首证,Tomas Rokicki 用陪集求解器算出完整距离分布并公布 39,248 个距离 12 的位置(dist12.txt,本站用作求解器的精确对账集);Michael Gottlieb + Ben Whitmore 的 OptClock 与 Shuang Chen 的 ClockSolver.java 是两份独立的单状态最优求解器。四份代码原样收藏在 solver/reference/clock/(只读、不编译);本站 lib/clock-solver.ts 为独立实现,未取用其代码
en: The proof that God's number for Clock is 12 and the full-space analysis: first proven by Jakob Kogler (2014); Tomas Rokicki computed the complete distance distribution with a coset solver and published all 39,248 distance-12 positions (dist12.txt — used here as an exact regression oracle); OptClock (Michael Gottlieb + Ben Whitmore) and ClockSolver.java (Shuang Chen) are two independent single-position optimal solvers. All four are archived verbatim under solver/reference/clock/ (read-only, never compiled); our lib/clock-solver.ts is an independent implementation and uses none of their code
long_en: Prior art for optimally solving the Rubik's Clock. Jakob Kogler (2014) first proved God's number is 12 using a one-side lookup table plus iterative-deepening DFS. Tomas Rokicki then computed the complete distance distribution over all 1,283,918,464,548,864 states with a coset solver (subgroup fixing the front cross, 248,832 cosets reduced to 9,906 by mirror / rotation / coprime-multiplication symmetry, ~3 days on a couple of desktops) and published both his source (clockcoset11.cpp) and the 39,248 distance-12 positions (dist12.txt). OptClock by Michael Gottlieb (qqwref) with a Qt GUI by Ben Whitmore is the two-phase single-position optimal solver used to verify those positions. Shuang Chen's ClockSolver.java (GPLv3) is an independent Java optimal solver. All are archived read-only under solver/reference/clock/ with a README explaining each algorithm; dist12.txt is wired into our test suite so the hardest depth bucket is verified exactly rather than by sampling
